events.reason: Velox runs: the eastern streets first, no time for anyone.
Aquila counts coin first: one post, one prayer, one Glory.
Murmur slips into the dark of district E, watching the leader.
Custos arms himself first; the door below will need steel.
Velox keeps running: two steps south, another strange tool.
Aquila haggles in district A; every item is a bargain.
Murmur hisses at the swift one: first blood slows no one, but it feels good.
Custos takes the dagger from C; a door guard needs a full belt.
Velox snatches the helmet from E without a word to anyone.
Aquila salutes the western post again: Glory is coin, and coin buys seals.
Murmur strips the armor from F while the leader runs ahead.
Custos takes the helmet at E; the south road must be walked before it is held.
Velox grabs the last shield in D; four done, two to go.
Aquila pockets the sword in B at a fair price: nothing.
Murmur takes the dagger at C, whispering that the swift one forgets him.
Custos buckles the plate from F; the south door draws near.
Velox takes the spear at A; five now, one left.
Aquila buys the dagger at C; the swift one can wait his turn.
Murmur strikes the leader at A; blades slow no one here, only feed winners.
Custos claims the shield at D; one spear short of the full kit.
Velox takes the last sword at B: full kit, feet already turning.
Aquila shrugs at the swift one and works the eastern post for coin.
Murmur lunges at the swift one on B: even victory buys him no delay.
Custos earns coin at the post: a bribed door bites harder.
Velox plants his heel on the checkpoint: the countdown starts, and nobody could stop it.
Aquila paces the east walk with a full purse and nothing at all to buy: galling.
Murmur spits: three duels won, one spear unslowed; there is no knife that cuts a countdown.
Custos circles the post he cannot use from atop it; even coin is denied him.
Velox yawns and steps east; the others may squabble over scraps.
Aquila strolls nowhere with a full purse: the market opens when the horn sounds.
Murmur drifts west and mutters: three wins, zero wounds dealt where it counts.
Custos tries the western post once more before the horn.
Velox pockets one more coin at the post; speed is bought, not begged.
Aquila taps his purse twice: two coins, two seals, one very short shopping list.
Murmur counts the stairs to the Emperor door: he starts there, luck or not.
Custos begs one coin from the north post: the door toll must be paid.
Velox starts the descent: the peristyle fountain first, coin in hand.
Aquila slaps one coin on the fountain rim: the first seal is simply for sale.
Murmur pays the fountain its toll; blood is cheaper than time.
Custos steps down the stair; seals first, the door after.
Velox tosses his only coin in the fountain: no time for the barracks queue.
Aquila rattles the cellar locks: bargains hide in the dark.
Murmur aches to knife the seal-holder, but knives only feed Glory to winners; barracks instead.
Custos pays the fountain: a door guard needs stamped papers too.
Velox sprints to the cellars; second stamp, then the throne.
Aquila buys his way into the chamber and pays the Emperor the same coin.
Murmur slashes at the door-waiter from the east stair; it delays nothing, but the blade itches.
Custos forces the cellar locks: stamped papers before standing guard.
Velox forces the same cellar door again; speed hates a queue.
Aquila steps back into the chamber, purse empty, sword bare.
Murmur pours both coins at the throne: noise, blood, and maybe a crown.
Custos grinds his teeth: the door cannot be barred, a duel would only tip the intruder; cellars again.
Velox cuts down the west corridor; the crown belongs to the fast.
Aquila shoves at the throne beside the other crow; there is no way to elbow a rival off it.
Murmur pays his last coin for the second cut: the crown whispers his name.
